note:
tenants takes 1.4.5. Two releases are crossed, 1.4.3 to 1.4.5, and 1.4.4 is
skipped. The apply writes 1.4.5's changelog entry and then back-fills 1.4.4's
below it, so a claw's own record carries both.

The releases: 1.4.4 and 1.4.5 are both class fix, disruption quiet. No core
floor moves in either. Codex stays at 0.147.0 and Claude stays at 2.1.227, the
same values 1.4.3 declared.

1.4.4 carries no landing section. Its errata paragraph says that every release
before it emptied the machine-wide skill directory of anything the release did
not carry, and that a claw who lost a skill that way has to put it back after
the update. A claw on this tier that placed a skill there itself before 1.4.4
should read that paragraph.

More than one claw reads this pointer, and the box readings below describe one
box: the one this promotion rides attended, with a person standing at it, in the
same beat this pointer moves. The order a later release makes possible is that
the tier's first claw rides the tag before the pointer moves at all. It needs
the ride flag, which arrives with this release, so the claws on this tier cannot
use it yet. Its claw-members group holds two people. Both have the persistent-session core
installed and both read 2.1.227, which meets the floor, and both read codex
0.147.0. No member reads as below a floor, so that claw's own classifier does
not defer the release to the quiet window. Its machine-wide skill directory held
the shipped skill alone, so nothing of its own was at stake in the apply. A
claw on this tier whose members or skill directory differ takes its own reading
before it lets the release land.

A claw carrying its own skills in the machine-wide tier now passes its apply.
1.4.4 is the release that did not. It shipped the fix that keeps those skills,
and the sibling control in the same phase took its expected count from the
manifest while reading the tier, so the run failed on every claw that had such a
skill. From 1.4.5 that control reads the tier three times and passes on a delta
of one, whatever the tier already holds. Its line says how many entries the core
sees there that the release did not install, and says those are the claw's own.

The control has two arms no claw has exercised. One fires when a claw's own
entry carries a name the manifest also declares. The other fires when the tier
reads short of what the release installed. Both are driven in the build
repository's own harness against fixture counts. Reaching either on a live claw
means damage to it, so they stay harness-proven.

The ride flag arrives with this apply and is not used by it. From 1.4.5 the
updater takes commonclaw-update.sh --release TAG, which rides a named release
from a channel at or below the claw's own. It refuses a tag no such channel
carries, and it refuses a run nobody is standing at. The updater a claw on this
tier runs today is 1.4.3's and has no such flag, so this promotion moves the
pointer first, the way every promotion before it did. The first ride from a tag
is a later release's business.

The line at the top of a ride names one channel once. On a first-tier claw it
says the claw's own pointer carried the tag. On a lower tier it names the
channel it read. Only the wording changed, and a ride resolves the same tag from
the same channel it did before.
